chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abi Jameela, from Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed a sword to a man, and it was in a sheath, and upon it were ornaments. So the inheritors said to him, 'For you is only the blade, and the wealth (ornaments) is not for you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but the sword with whatever is in it is for him.'

He (the narrator) said, 'So I said, 'A man bequeathed a container to a man, and there was wealth in it. So the inheritors said, 'For you is only the container, and the wealth is not for you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The container with whatever is in it is for him.''
ai.seo_question: Does a bequeathed sword include its sheath and ornaments, or just the blade?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes the principle of 'al-maqtul bihi ma'a al-maqbul' (the bequeathed item includes its contents) by distinguishing between the sword's sheath and the chest's contents, ensuring the beneficiary receives the full value intended. This ruling, recorded in *Al-Kafi*, resolves disputes where heirs attempt to limit bequests to the container or specific part, affirming that the general term implies the whole unless restricted. It underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on honoring the testator's apparent intent in property transfers.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Abu Jameela, 
(It has been narrated) from Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who bequeathed a sword to a man, and it was in a sheath, and upon it were ornaments. So the inheritors said to him, ‘But rather, for you is the blade, and the wealth (ornaments) is not for you’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, but the sword with whatever it was it, is for him’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So I said, ‘A man bequeathed a container and there used to be wealth in it. So the inheritors said, ‘But rather, for you is the container and the wealth is not for you’. So Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The container along with whatever is in it, is for him’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from abu Jamilah who has narrated the following: “I once asked al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who has made a will for a man about a sword which is in a cover (sword sheathing) with decorations on it. The heirs said that only the sword is for him and not the asset (the valuable decorations). He (the Imam) said, ‘The sword and that in which it is belongs to him.’

I then asked about the case of a man who makes a will about a box for a man. The heirs say that only the box without its contents belongs to him. ‘Not only the box but its contents also belong to him’, said abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam .”
